Planting in elevated pots can reduce animal bites. My cherry tomatoes still got nailed by sneaky chipmunks, though. At least, I think they were chipmunks.

Easy plants: Cherry tomatoes, jalapenos, parsley and string beans

Corn, potatoes, okra, maters, crook neck squash, canteloupes, watermelon, greens, onions, peppers, and more okra. Don't worry about organic only, just buy some fertilizer. Compost is nice too, but ammonia nitrate works too well to not use.

Make sure to till the ground really good and give everything enough space.

Where do you live? Do you have pests, deer, ground squirrels that sort of thing?

Tomatoes are fun, squashes/pumpkins are deer resistant but maybe not other nibbly critters.

Potatoes, carrots, beans, peas are all pretty easy.

Your local nursery or co op would be the best place for help.

Zucchini and summer squash are easy and prolific. Plant one of each person in the household, and give them lots of space.

I also agree with other suggestions here, radishes are easy and quick. Cherry tomatoes are a good choice for someone starting out because the fruit matures quickly. I have trouble getting a full size tomato to turn red before something happens to it, either rot, birds, bugs, etc.

Also go down to your local feed store to see if they sell plants they started from seed. They will be happy to give you all kinds of advice on what grows well in your area. Plus if they harvest their own seeds to replant, they will have plants that are specifically adapted to your local climate.

Which brings me to another point, save the seeds from you best plants. Plant them the following year. Repeat year after year. Through the use of natural selection you will have your own personally bred plants that will perform best in your personal garden.
